paragraphs.text: Lit., “a throwing down [of seed].” Gr., ka·ta·bo·lesʹ.
Or, “without blemish before him. For in love (5) he foreordained.”
Lit., “house administration; household management.” Gr., oi·ko·no·miʹan; Lat., di·spen·sa·ti·oʹnem. See Lu 12:42 ftn.
“To gather . . . together again.” According to G. H. Thayer’s Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament, fourth ed. (1901), p. 39, “to bring together again for himself.”
Or, “earnest money (down payment) in advance.” Gr., ar·ra·bonʹ; J18,22(Heb.), ʽe·ra·vohnʹ. See 2Co 1:22 ftn.
Or, “order of things.” Gr., ai·oʹni; Lat., saeʹcu·lo; J17,18,22(Heb.), ba·ʽoh·lamʹ haz·zehʹ, “in this order of things.”
Or, “order of things.” Gr., ai·oʹna; Lat., saeʹcu·lum; J17(Heb.), dohr, “period; age; generation”; J18(Heb.), kemin·haghʹ, “according to the custom.”
Or, “orders of things.” Gr., ai·oʹsin; Lat., saeʹcu·lis.
“In the world.” Gr., en toi koʹsmoi; J17,22(Heb.), ba·ʽoh·lamʹ.

Lit., “middle wall.” An allusion to the wall in the area of the temple that fenced off the unsanctified Gentile worshipers from entering the inner courtyards that were open only to the sanctified Jewish worshipers. According to the Mishnah (translated by Danby, 1950, p. 592), the stone barrier was called “the Soreg.” This wall was said to be 1.3 m (4.3 ft) high. See App 9F; see also ad under “Temple,” subheading, “Court of the Gentiles.”
“Foundation.” Gr., the·me·liʹoi, dative, sing.; Lat., fun·da·menʹtum.
Or, “divine habitation (dwelling).” Gr., na·onʹ; Lat., temʹplum; J22(Heb.), heh·khalʹ, “palace; temple.”
Lit., “what is the house administration of the mystery (sacred secret).”
Or, “may be filled up to all.”
Or, “consisting of men,” in agreement with M (Ps 68:18) and LXX (Ps 67:19). Lit., “to the men.”
Or, “he might bring all things to fulfillment.”
Or, “to the putting into proper alignment.”
“To loose conduct.” Gr., tei a·sel·geiʹai, dative, sing. See Ga 5:19 ftn, “Conduct.”
Lit., “to the spirit of your mind.”
Or, “covetousness.” Lit., “having more,” that is, a desire to have more; insatiableness. Gr., ple·o·ne·xiʹa.
“Of Jehovah,” J7,8; אD(Gr.), tou Ky·riʹou; AVgcSyp, “of God”; B, “of our Lord”; P46, “of the Christ.” See App 1D.
“In union with [the] Lord,” P46אADcVgSyh,pArm; BD* omit.
Lit., “not be you provoking to wrath.”
Or, “crafty acts.” Gr., me·tho·diʹas; Lat., in·siʹdi·as.
Lit., “the panoply.” Gr., ten pa·no·pliʹan; Lat., ar·ma·tuʹram.
“With the equipment.” Lit., “in readiness; in preparedness.”
